description.en-US: Personal F-Droid repository with custom apps: Pluralis (alternative news aggregator) and OpenLibe Extended (e-ink library client).

summary.en-US: Convert videos to 320 kbps MP3 files and share them

description.en-US:
An app that does one thing: turn videos into MP3 files.

Pick one or more videos, and each one's audio track is extracted and
re-encoded to a 320 kbps CBR MP3 saved in your Downloads folder. When
it is done you get a list of the files, each with a Share button — so
sending them to a cloud folder, Telegram, WhatsApp or anywhere else
is one tap away.

* 320 kbps constant bitrate, encoded with LAME
* Batch conversion — pick as many videos as you like
* Saved straight to Downloads, visible in your file manager
* Share individual files or all of them at once
* Works with anything your phone can play: MP4, MKV, WebM, 3GP…
* Videos can also be sent to the app from another app's share sheet
* Conversion keeps running when you leave the app

No accounts, no network access, no ads, no tracking. Everything
happens on the device.

Bundles LAME 3.100 (LGPL-2.1-or-later).

summary.en-US: Audio-only YouTube subscription player, 100% text

description.en-US:
Sobre is an anti-brainrot audio player for YouTube subscriptions.
It plays only the audio from channels you explicitly follow —
no video, no thumbnails, no algorithmic recommendations, no Shorts,
no comments, no infinite scroll.

The interface is 100% text: no images, no icons, no avatars.
Subscribe by pasting a channel or video URL, or by sharing directly
from the YouTube app.

Features:
* Audio-only playback with background and lock screen support
* Subscribe to channels via URL paste or Android share intent
* Chronological feed — no algorithm, no recommendations
* Episode chapters and full descriptions
* Adjustable playback speed (0.75x to 2x)
* Download episodes for offline listening
* Periodic RSS-based feed refresh
* High-contrast text UI, e-ink friendly
* Fully local, no accounts, no tracking

Built with NewPipeExtractor (GPLv3). Not affiliated with YouTube.

summary.en-US: Dictionnaire Littré complet, gratuit et hors-ligne

description.en-US:
Le dictionnaire de la langue fran\xE7aise d'\xC9mile Littr\xE9,
complet et enti\xE8rement gratuit, consultable hors-ligne.

Widget d'\xE9cran d'accueil \xAB Mot du jour \xBB, et mot du jour expos\xE9 aux
autres applications (tuile de Reader's Launcher).
78 599 entr\xE9es avec d\xE9finitions, \xE9tymologies et citations.
Recherche instantan\xE9e, mot du jour, favoris, renvois crois\xE9s
cliquables, mode sombre. Aucune connexion internet requise.
Donn\xE9es lexicographiques sous licence CC BY-SA 3.0
(Fran\xE7ois Gannaz, littre.org).

summary.en-US: Unofficial espresso timer for the 9Barista stovetop machine. 3 taps only.

description.en-US:
A minimal espresso timer designed for the 9Barista double-boiler stovetop
espresso machine. Unofficial and fan-made — not affiliated with or endorsed
by 9Barista Ltd.

Three taps per brew:
1. Tap to start heating (counts up, warns at 8 minutes)
2. Tap when espresso appears — starts extraction timer with circular
   progress ring, turns green in the 25–30 second target zone
3. Tap when done — shows results and grind adjustment advice

Haptic feedback at 25s (target zone), 30s (over target), and 8 min
(max heating). Screen stays on during brewing.

Timings based on official 9Barista recommendations:
• Heating: 3–6 minutes typical
• Extraction: 25–30 seconds
• Target output: 35–40g

No ads. No tracking. No accounts. No permissions beyond vibration.

summary.en-US: Minimalist 4-minute guided box breathing exercise

description.en-US:
A calming, distraction-free breathing exercise app. Follow the
animated guide around a square: breathe in, hold, breathe out, hold.
The 4-minute session starts with a 3-second rhythm and gently
transitions to 4 seconds halfway through. Bilingual instructions
(English / French). No accounts, no ads, no tracking.

summary.en-US: ePub reader tuned for daily newspaper / magazine issues

description.en-US:
Fork of Book's Story (ua.acclorite.book_story) with an opinionated
magazine-mode parser and TOC for ePub issues produced by the in-house
newsletter generator (NZZ, 24 heures, Courrier International, Economist
fixtures).

Detects magazine ePubs at open time, paginates the table of contents
with one card per article (category, title, optional cover image),
and routes tap → article view rendered by an in-zip WebView.

A permanent three-zone navigation header (prev / home / next) sits on
top of the existing tap-zone gesture system on every magazine screen.

Installs next to upstream Book's Story under its own application id
(com.freedomfighter.magazinereader since 0.2.24; the earlier
ua.acclorite.book_story.debug builds must be uninstalled by hand).

summary.en-US: E-ink optimized e-book reader and library browser

description.en-US:
Open-source e-book reader optimized for e-ink displays. Paginated
EPUB reading with adaptive font sizing, high-contrast themes, and
tap zones designed for e-paper. Search and download from online
library catalogs. Local library management.
This application is a reading tool. It does not host any content.
Users are solely responsible for compliance with copyright laws
in their jurisdiction.

summary.en-US: Plain black-and-white audio player that transcribes on the phone, in the language and quality you choose

description.en-US:
Plays audio files and resumes each one where it was left. Standard
Media3 playback: media notification with −5 s, play/pause, +10 s and
stop, lock screen and Bluetooth buttons, speed 0.8× to 2×. Transcribes
on the phone with whisper.cpp into plain .txt files in
Documents/Transcriptions, which any reader opens. Share the audio or
the transcript, or save a copy to any folder. Widget: the last file
played, one tap to resume. Text only, six languages.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white e-book reader with a shelf

description.en-US:
A shelf of books as a plain list, and pages of plain text cut at whole
lines. EPUB, MOBI, FB2 and text files, opened from the app, a file manager
or a share. Tap halves to turn pages, long press for chapters and text
size. Position remembered per book. White on black or black on white.

summary.en-US: Search free ebook catalogues, files to the phone; reading left to the reader

description.en-US:
A black-and-white search-and-download app for free ebooks: Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks,
Wikisource, the Bibliothèque numérique romande, Ebooks libres et gratuits, textos.info, the
Internet Archive's freely downloadable texts; Anna's Archive only once turned on after reading
what it is. The file goes to Download/Reader's Bookshop for Reader's Books or any reader. The
app hosts nothing: the user accepts once, and ticks before every search, that what is
downloaded is their responsibility; when a source tells the author's dates the app says whether
the seventy years have passed.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white, text-only calendar

description.en-US:
Reader's Calendar shows the phone's own calendars — the ones your accounts already
sync (Google, Infomaniak, Nextcloud…) — as plain text, white on black or black on
white. No colour codes: the calendar an event belongs to is named in a quiet line of
text on the event's page.

* Agenda: the coming days as a list. Month: a grid of numbers, a dot for days with
  events, today inverted. Week: a list in portrait, a time grid in landscape.
* Event page with location and description; create and edit events with reminder,
  repetition, all-day, calendar choice.
* Landscape puts the month grid beside the agenda and splits event pages in two.
* Can be the default calendar app, including for Reader's Launcher's agenda tile.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes. No account, no network of its own.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white, text-only RSS reader

description.en-US:
The latest articles of your RSS and Atom sources as a plain list, read as
pages cut at whole lines. Sources, saved articles, OPML and paid Substacks.
White on black or black on white, no icons, no colours; pages instead of
scrolling for e-ink screens. Born from Pluralis.

summary.en-US: A food journal made of photos

description.en-US:
Photograph what you are about to eat, as thoughtlessly as you would reach
into a bowl of peanuts. The widget, the quick-settings tile or the app's
big button open the viewfinder; a touch anywhere (or a volume key) takes
the photo and the screen closes by itself. Each photo is labelled
breakfast, lunch, dinner or snack from the time it was taken. The home
screen is one folder per day. Physical activity in one tap: strength
training, intense activity, endurance, or a line of your own. Your weight
once a day, with a curve of how it moves. Everything
stays on the phone: no network permission, no account. Export the journal
as one zip to carry it to a new phone; importing adds and replaces
nothing. Black and white, text only, six languages.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white, text-only launcher in the spirit of the Light Phone

description.en-US:
Reader's Launcher turns the home screen into a single column of words. No icons,
no colours, no wallpaper: white on black, or black on white — flip between the two
with a double tap, from the "Reader's theme" quick-settings tile, or in settings.

* The home screen is one fixed page that never scrolls. Tiles are plain text: an app,
  or a category that opens a text list of apps.
* A grid of 3 to 5 squares pinned at the bottom holds the unavoidable apps (phone,
  messages…) with their icons rendered as monochrome glyphs.
* Built-in widgets: clock; weather (Open-Meteo, no account, tap for five days);
  agenda (next event, swipe for the following ones); tasks (first task of a list
  from Reader's Tasks or Tasks.org, swipe for the following ones, tick to complete,
  + to add). Standard app widgets can be added too.
* Swipe up for the alphabetical app list with search and the usual long-press
  actions (add to home, category, rename, hide, app info, uninstall).
* Swipe up and hold on the home screen for a text list of recently used apps.
* Swipe down for notifications. Export and import the whole setup as a JSON file.
* Two books beside the home screen: swipe right or left to open one (EPUB, MOBI, FB2,
  plain text), tap to turn pages; each book reopens where you stopped.
* English by default; French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian follow the
  device language.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes; left or centred. No ads, no tracking.

summary.en-US: A bowl every X minutes, a timed meditation, bowls at set times

description.en-US:
Three things a meditator asks of a bowl, black and white, text only:
a single strike every X minutes until you stop it, a meditation of X
minutes closed by three bowls, and one or three bowls at set times every
day. Retreat Timer's five bowls or your own mp3/wav. Bowls are armed as
exact alarm-clock alarms and rung by a foreground service, so they sound
on time through Doze and silent mode. Home-screen widget (play/stop,
minutes, countdown, progress) and a Reader's Launcher tile.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white plain-text notes, synced over WebDAV

description.en-US:
One list, one page. A note is a text file whose first line is its title.
Notes live in a WebDAV folder (kDrive, Nextcloud…) as plain .txt files,
synced both ways with conflict copies. White on black or black on white,
no formatting, no folders, no colours. Shared text becomes a note.

summary.en-US: Podcasts in black and white — subscribe, download, listen, nothing else

description.en-US:
A podcast player with nothing on the screen but lines of text. Subscribe by pasting the
address of a feed or by sharing a link to the app; the episodes wait in one of three lists —
what is on the phone or already begun, what is new across all the channels, or one channel at
a time. An episode is downloaded or played straight over the connection, resumes exactly where
it was left, and once heard through is marked and its file let go.

Subscriptions travel as OPML, which any podcast app reads, and the settings — with the place
each episode was left — as a JSON file. Those two files are the whole of the synchronisation
with the desktop twin: there is no server and no account, and nothing leaves the phone but the
requests to the feeds themselves.

English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian; white on black or black on white,
three fonts, three text sizes.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white voice recorder that transcribes on the phone (whisper.cpp); optional cloud folder

description.en-US:
Record a memo, a lecture or a conversation with one tap (list, widget,
Reader's Launcher tile). Nothing leaves the phone by default. Set up a
WebDAV folder (kDrive, Nextcloud) in three questions and each recording
goes there, where a small worker on your own computer cleans the sound,
normalises its loudness and transcribes it with WhisperX; the transcript
and the cleaned audio come back to the phone. Text only, white on black
or black on white, six languages.

summary.en-US: Black-and-white, text-only CalDAV task lists

description.en-US:
Reader's Tasks shows the open tasks of a CalDAV list — Infomaniak, Nextcloud,
Tasks.org Cloud, Radicale, any server that stores VTODO — as plain text, white on
black or black on white. Tick a box to complete, tap the line at the bottom to add,
long press for rename, due tomorrow, delete. "show n done" brings completed tasks
back so a box ticked by mistake can be reopened. Lists can be hidden and reordered.

It is the task app behind the tasks tile of Reader's Launcher: the launcher reads
and writes the lists directly, with no permission prompt, since both apps are signed
with the same key. The desktop twin for Linux lives at
github.com/funkypitt/readers-tasks.

Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes. No account with the app itself, no
tracking: your server, your app password, stored on the phone only.

summary.en-US: Plays retreat recordings offline, with nothing able to interrupt them

description.en-US:
Retreat Player plays MP3s of dhamma talks, bells, and chanting during a
meditation retreat — built on the same principle as Retreat Timer: once
playback starts, nothing interrupts it.

* Every recording is downloaded into the app's own storage when it is loaded,
  so playback needs no network — airplane mode is fine.
* Playback runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock: the system
  cannot kill or pause it, even with the screen off for an hour-long talk.
* The screen stays on while a recording plays — no lock, no screensaver —
  showing the progress the whole time.
* A recording plays only because you pressed play, and only once: when it
  ends, nothing else starts automatically.

Loading and organising:

* Tap + to load recordings from the phone, from a shared kDrive folder
  (public link — read-only, no password), or from a podcast feed; the link
  and feed URLs are remembered for next time.
* Tiles are filed into two sections — Bells & chanting on top (used every
  day), then Dharma talks — and ordered by hand with arrows.
* The player shows elapsed and remaining time together, with play, pause,
  stop, 10-second jumps, and back-to-beginning.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts.

summary.en-US: Rings one or three meditation bells on schedule, even in deep sleep

description.en-US:
Retreat Timer rings a recording of singing-bowl bells at the times of day you
choose — the signal to begin or end a sitting — so a meditation retreat keeps
running on schedule even when the teacher is not present. Each time can ring
three bells or a single bell, whichever that moment in the day calls for.

Built for one job: the bells ring no matter what.

* Exact alarms via the same mechanism the stock Clock app uses, so they fire on
  time even when the device is locked, asleep, or in Doze for hours.
* A foreground service holds a wake lock and plays through the alarm stream, so
  the system cannot mute or kill the bells mid-ring.
* Alarms are re-armed automatically after a reboot, time change, or app update.
* A readiness light turns green once battery optimisation and notifications are
  set, so the teacher can leave knowing the schedule is safe.

Easy to set up:

* Tap Add bell and pick the time. The picker opens ready for typing, so any
  minute is set directly — 06:47, not just 06:45 — with a dial one tap away.
* In that same picker, choose three bells or one for this time — three to open
  and close a sitting, one for the smaller markers in a day. Preview either
  before setting it. The schedule shows a small x3 or x1 badge beside every
  bell, so which rings which is readable at a glance.
* Tap any time to edit it — and its number of bells; toggle bells on or off;
  delete with one tap.
* Four bell sounds to choose from — singing bell, Tibetan E flat bowl, gong
  bowl and Satipanya — all matched to the same loudness, so switching changes
  the timbre and never the volume. One bell and three bells are matched too.
* Bell volume and talk volume are set separately, because a spoken recording
  normally has to be much louder than a bowl strike to fill the same room.
  Each has its own Test button that plays at the exact level the room will
  hear. Test bell rings once, which is all it takes to judge the level, and
  Test talk uses the talk that is actually coming up next.

Dharma talk library:

* Add talks from this phone, an Infomaniak kDrive public share link, or a
  podcast RSS feed — every import is downloaded into the app so playback works
  with no network at all.
* Play a talk instantly, or schedule one to play at a set time exactly like a
  bell.
* A player bar with a draggable progress bar — talks often open with minutes
  of silence, so drag straight to the speech instead of waiting it out.
  Restart, 10 seconds back and forward, pause, and both elapsed and remaining
  time, from the app or the notification.
* Optional "keep Bluetooth speaker awake": portable speakers disconnect after
  a few minutes of silence, so the next bell would come faintly from the
  tablet. Turn it on when using an external speaker and it plays a
  barely-audible sound between bells to hold the link open. The bells are
  untouched — still the exact-alarm system, this is only a separate faint
  stream.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts. The schedule repeats every day.

summary.en-US: Rings a bell every so many minutes, until you stop it

description.en-US:
Retreat Walk rings a singing bowl at a fixed interval — every 10 minutes, say —
over and over until you stop it. For switching partners in a paired meditation
exercise, and for sitting with a regular reminder to stay awake.

One number and one button. That is the whole app.

* Set the minutes between bells and press Start. The bell rings at that many
  minutes, then at twice, then three times, and on and on.
* Press Stop in the app, or on the notification, and the session ends.
* The screen shows a countdown to the next bell and how many have rung.

It rings on time:

* Every bell is an exact alarm, the same mechanism the phone's own Clock app
  uses, so it fires even when the device is locked, asleep or in power-saving
  Doze.
* The session runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock, so the system
  cannot mute the bowl or kill it partway through.
* Bells are timed from the start of the session rather than from the previous
  bell, so an hour in they have not drifted away from the clock.
* The notification is silent and carries a Stop action — the bowl is the only
  sound the app ever makes, which is what a quiet room needs.

The bell is a single strike of the Satipanya bowl, shared with Retreat Timer.

No ads, no tracking, no accounts, and no network permission at all.

summary.en-US: Classic artillery game rebuilt for mobile. 2-player local and online.

description.en-US:
Tank Wars Mobile is a faithful recreation of the classic DOS artillery game
Tank Wars 3.2 (1992) by Kenneth Morse, rebuilt from the ground up for mobile
touchscreens.

Two players take turns aiming their tanks and firing an arsenal of weapons at
each other across randomly generated destructible terrain. Judge the angle,
power, and wind to land your shots — there's no trajectory preview, so every
shot is a test of skill and intuition.

16 weapons including nukes, MIRVs, lasers, and chain reaction inducers.
3 defense systems: shields, inertia dampeners, and repulsers.
6 wall types, 5 wind levels, destructible terrain with crumbling.
Local 2-player hot-seat and online multiplayer via Firebase.

Free and open source. No ads. No tracking. No in-app purchases.

summary.en-US: 16 multiplayer games — play locally or online. No ads, no accounts.

description.en-US:
2P Games is a collection of 16 touch-friendly multiplayer games for two
players. Play locally on one device or online with a friend. No accounts,
no ads.

8 games support online play via room codes or quick match:
4 in a Row, Caro, Awalé, Memory, Duck-Day Chess, Tank Wars,
Word Clash, and Reversi.

Also includes Tennis (with power-ups), Pool, Carrom, Air Hockey,
Mini Golf, Star Clash, Hangman, and Horse Jump.

Each game has built-in instructions accessible via the ? button.

All games feature intuitive touch controls. Built-in calming background
music with toggle. Every game has rematch support.

Free and open source. No ads. No tracking. No in-app purchases.

summary.en-US: Local DNS VPN that blocks social networks

description.en-US:
Reader's Detox blocks social networks on the device with a local DNS VPN.
No account, no server: the filtering happens on the phone, also on IPv6-only carriers.
Black and white and text only, like the other Reader's apps; six languages.

Pierre Gallaz · developed with Claude Code.
